title: AudienceCircle
description: A consent-based, location-independent audience circle (household or community). It is an access-control scope for explicitly granted private nodes, not a map object. The top level describes the canonical PostgreSQL record (domain_audience_circles). A circle never becomes public: the only HTTP projection is own_circle, returned to an account that is itself invited to or an active member of the circle. No member of a forming circle gains content rights.

name.description: 1 to 80 Unicode code points, trimmed with Rust Unicode White_Space semantics, without control characters (U+FEFF is not whitespace for Rust). The API defaults to 'Hausgemeinschaft' or 'Gemeinschaft'. The database CHECK enforces only the length bound; trimming and the control-character rule are enforced by the HTTP handler, the only writer.

state.description: forming: founder active, founding invitation pending, nobody has content rights. active: became active when a second non-disabled member confirmed, and stays active while at least one active member remains (a circle can therefore be active with a single member). inactive: terminal; the founding proposal had no pending invitation left, or the last active member left. The API never moves a circle out of inactive.

created_by_account_id.description: Founder account. NULL after that account is deleted. Never part of an HTTP response.

own_circle.description: Response item of GET /api/circles/me and the body of POST /api/circles (201) and POST /api/circles/{id}/accept (200). Visible only to the account named by the membership row. It carries no member list, founder, inviter or creation time.

membership_status.description: The reader's own membership. An invitation never grants content rights.

invitation_created_at.description: Creation instant of the reader's pending membership row. Clients echo it as expected_invitation_created_at so a stale accept or decline cannot act on a later re-invitation. NULL unless membership_status is invited.

own_circle_page.description: GET /api/circles/me: newest first by (created_at, id), at most 100 items. The next page is requested with after=<id of the last item>. A shorter page is the last page.
